_notes: PILOT ONLY — 2026-08-04. NOT wired into anything and NOT merged into heritage-content.json; the live heritage schema is untouched so the existing panel cannot break while this is reviewed. 20 railways sampled STRATIFIED BY TYPE (11 operating, 3 museum, 3 funicular, 3 tramway) rather than alphabetically, because the article shape differs sharply by type and an A-Z sample would have been almost all 'operating'. Every value is quoted from the article text in `source`; nothing is inferred. Blank means the article does not state it.
method: en.wikipedia.org action=query&prop=extracts&explaintext, first 6000 chars, via the wikipedia_title already stored in heritage-content.json

alford-valley-railway.source: 'construction of the Alford Valley Railway started in 1856 and the line opened in 1859 as a GNSR branch line'; 'The narrow gauge railway... proposed in 1979 and opened in 1980'
alford-valley-railway._flag: THREE opening events, not two: original 1859, narrow-gauge heritage line 1980, and a further re-opening in August 2023 after six years closed. The schema has nowhere to put the third.

aln-valley-railway.source: 'The line opened on 5 August 1850, both to freight and passenger traffic'; 'formally opened by the Duke of Northumberland on 30 October 2013'

amerton-railway._flag: NEW BUILD, never a mainline — a narrow-gauge line laid on a greenfield site. opened_year here means 'opened as the heritage railway it is', the opposite of what the field means elsewhere. heritage_reopened_year is not blank-because-unknown, it is not applicable.

avon-valley-railway.source: no original opening year stated in the article extract
avon-valley-railway._flag: Original Bristol-Mangotsfield-Bath line date absent. '2024 marked the 50th anniversary since the first trains ran' would give 1974 for the heritage reopening BY ARITHMETIC — left blank rather than derived, per the sourcing rule.

bala-lake-railway.source: 'The railway, which opened in August 1868, was built by the Bala and Dolgelley Railway Company'; 'Bala Lake Railway opened on 13 August 1972'

bluebell-railway.source: 'the northern half of the Lewes and East Grinstead Railway... opened in 1882'; 'Preservationists successfully launched a rescued operation... on 7 August 1960'

brecon-mountain-railway.source: 'The railway opened to passengers in June 1980'
brecon-mountain-railway._flag: 1980 is the HERITAGE opening. The original Brecon & Merthyr line's date is not in the extract, so opened_year is blank.

bristol-harbour-railway.source: 'the first part of the network opened in 1872 between Temple Meads and the Floating Harbour'; 'In 1978, a heritage railway named the Bristol Harbour Railway was opened'

bure-valley-railway.source: 'the East Norfolk Railway opened from Norwich to Cromer [1877], with an extension from Wroxham to Aylsham in 1880'; 'The Bure Valley Railway opened on 10 July 1990'
bure-valley-railway._flag: TWO candidate original years. 1877 is the parent ENR (Norwich-Cromer); 1880 is the Wroxham-Aylsham extension, which is the trackbed the BVR actually occupies. Took 1880 — flag if the parent company's date is preferred.

caledonian-railway-brechin.source: 'since 1993 trains have run at weekends during the summer'
caledonian-railway-brechin._flag: Article extract is dominated by a locomotive roster; no original Caledonian Railway opening date appears. 1993 is a 'trains have run since' phrasing rather than a stated opening.

cambrian-heritage-railway.source: no opening year of either kind in the extract
cambrian-heritage-railway._flag: Extract covers only the 2009 trust merger and restoration works. Neither the original Cambrian Railways opening nor a heritage reopening is stated.

almond-valley-heritage-centre.source: article extract is 916 characters and contains no year-bearing sentence
almond-valley-heritage-centre._flag: Effectively a stub for this purpose.

amberley-museum-railway.source: 'A running line was built at Amberley from 1982 to 1984'
amberley-museum-railway._flag: MUSEUM railway, never a mainline. The only date is a construction SPAN (1982-1984), not an opening, and the museum's own opening date is separate and not given. Both fields left blank.

barrow-hill-roundhouse.source: 'Staveley Roundhouse was built to a standard Midland Railway square shed design in 1870'; 'The site reopened to the public in July 1998'
barrow-hill-roundhouse._flag: 1870 is 'built', not 'opened' — for a locomotive shed those are usually the same year, but it is a wording difference worth noting.

aberystwyth-cliff-railway.source: 'The Aberystwyth Cliff Railway opened on 1 August 1896'
aberystwyth-cliff-railway._flag: Continuously operating funicular — never closed, so there is no heritage reopening. The 1998 charity purchase is an ownership change, not a reopening.

babbacombe-cliff-railway.source: 'Construction started in 1924, and the line was first opened on 1 April 1926'
babbacombe-cliff-railway._flag: THREE reopenings in the article (1951 after wartime closure, July 2023 after repairs) and none is a heritage reopening — this is a working funicular, not a preserved line. Picking any of them would misrepresent it.

bridgnorth-cliff-railway.source: 'The railway was opened on 7 July 1892 by Mayor John Anderson'
bridgnorth-cliff-railway._flag: 1944 re-opening was electrification, 2024 was repair. Neither is a heritage reopening.

central-tramway-scarborough.source: 'Built in just 6 months between January and August 1881, the Tramway opened on Monday 1 August'

crich-tramway.source: timeline: '1963 - First horse tram service at what was then the Crich Tramway Museum'
crich-tramway._flag: MUSEUM, never a mainline. 1963 is the museum's first service. Also note the site sits on a mineral railway built by George Stephenson, whose date is not given — so 'original opening' is genuinely undefined here.

east-anglian-transport-museum-tramway.source: 'the museum opened to the public on 28 May 1972'
east-anglian-transport-museum-tramway._flag: MUSEUM, never a mainline. Its narrow-gauge railway opened separately in 1973, so even 'the' opening year is two-valued.
